subject.title: Per-agent tools.selfDeny — allow tool inheritance to subagents while denying direct use

question: Should OpenClaw add an explicit per-agent delegate-only/self-deny tool policy, and should it be modeled as `tools.selfDeny`, `delegateOnly`, a scoped allow annotation, or folded into per-spawn policy?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the requested behavior changes public config and the security boundary between requester-visible tools and child-delegable tools, so automation should not choose the permanent semantics or naming.

options.title: Approve explicit delegate-only config
options.body: Add an optional per-agent self-deny/delegate-only policy that hides tools from the requester's model surface while preserving normal deny-wins behavior for inherited child policy.

options.title: Fold into per-spawn policy only
options.body: Let per-spawn child restriction work own child scoping and document that parent direct-use prevention still needs separate agents or prompt guidance.

options.title: Reject parent-deny delegation
options.body: Keep monotonic policy unchanged and document the security rationale plus separate-agent workaround before closing this direction.

recommendation.title: Approve explicit delegate-only config
recommendation.body: Add an optional per-agent self-deny/delegate-only policy that hides tools from the requester's model surface while preserving normal deny-wins behavior for inherited child policy.
